Series::normal_¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series& Series::normal_() const
Series& Series::normal_(double mean) const
Series& Series::normal_(double mean, double stddev) const

What It Does¶

Overwrites every element of the receiver with an independent draw from a normal (Gaussian) distribution.

The receiver supplies the shape, dtype, platform, and storage; its current values play no part and are simply replaced. This is the in-place “fill this buffer with noise” primitive — the counterpart of the factory randn, which creates a new tensor from a shape you pass it. Reach for normal_ when a buffer already exists (a pre-allocated parameter, a reused scratch tensor, a slice of a larger array).

The three overloads set the two parameters:

call

mean

stddev

normal_()

0

1

normal_(m)

m

1

normal_(m, s)

m

s

stddev is the standard deviation, not the variance — normal_(0, 2) has variance 4. stddev = 0 is allowed and produces a deterministic fill with mean (a useful stand-in when a pipeline that normally samples needs to be made reproducible for a test).

Reproducibility¶

The draw is deterministic given the process-wide RNG seed. Call pluss::rng_seed(seed) before sampling and the exact sequence of values is fixed; two runs from the same seed produce equal tensors. Each sampling call advances a stream counter, so consecutive draws differ unless you reseed between them.

Parameters¶

mean (double, default 0): the center of the distribution. Must be finite.

stddev (double, default 1): the spread. Must be finite and >= 0.

Returns¶

Series& A reference to the receiver, now holding the samples. The write is in-place and preserves storage identity, so every alias of the receiver sees the new values.

Raises¶

  • if the receiver’s dtype is not floating-point or complex

  • if mean or stddev is non-finite, or stddev < 0

Gradient¶

Not differentiable. A random overwrite has no derivative with respect to the values it replaced or to mean / stddev.

Examples¶

Example 1. Fill a buffer with standard-normal samples. Seeded here, so the values are fixed.

pluss::rng_seed(42);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({5}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.normal_();
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x);

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0.4417, 0.3803, 0.3206, 1.6263, -1.0114]

Example 2. The same seed gives the same draw; without reseeding, the next call draws fresh values.

pluss::rng_seed(7);
auto a = pluss::series::empty({4}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64); a.normal_();
pluss::rng_seed(7);
auto b = pluss::series::empty({4}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64); b.normal_();
auto c = pluss::series::empty({4}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64); c.normal_();  // stream advanced
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "a == b (reseeded):     " << a.equal(b) << "\n"
          << "a == c (not reseeded): " << a.equal(c) << "\n";

Output¶

a == b (reseeded):     true
a == c (not reseeded): false

Example 3. mean and stddev place and scale the samples.

pluss::rng_seed(1);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({5}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.normal_(100.0, 0.1);
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x);

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[100.1179, 100.0694, 99.9451, 99.9794, 100.0126]

Every value sits within a few tenths of 100 — stddev = 0.1.

Example 4. Over a large sample, the empirical moments converge to the requested ones.

pluss::rng_seed(2024);
auto x = pluss::series::empty({200000}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.normal_(3.0, 2.0);
std::cout << "mean~" << x.mean().to_vec<double>()[0]
          << "  stddev~" << x.std().to_vec<double>()[0] << "\n";

Output¶

mean~3.00064  stddev~2.0055

A finite sample never matches exactly; the spread of these estimates shrinks like 1/sqrt(n).

Example 5. stddev = 0 is a valid degenerate fill — every element becomes mean.

auto x = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
x.normal_(5.0, 0.0);
pluss::series::print(std::cout, x);

Output¶

Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[5.0000, 5.0000, 5.0000]

Example 6. An integer receiver is rejected; so is a negative stddev.

try {
  auto i = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Int64);
  i.normal_();
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}
try {
  auto f = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
  f.normal_(0.0, -1.0);
} catch (const std::exception& e) {
  std::string m = e.what();
  std::cout << m.substr(0, m.find('\n')) << "\n";
}

Output¶

normal_: receiver must have a floating-point or complex dtype
normal_: expected finite parameters with std >= 0

For an integer buffer of random values, use random_.

Example 7. The fill is in-place — every alias of the receiver sees it.

pluss::rng_seed(9);
auto base = pluss::series::empty({3}, pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
auto alias = base;
base.normal_();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "alias.is_set_to(base): " << alias.is_set_to(base) << "\n";
std::cout << "alias = ";
pluss::series::print(std::cout, alias);

Output¶

alias.is_set_to(base): true
alias = Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[1.9341, 1.0008, 1.9234]

The factory randn would instead return a new tensor and leave base untouched.

Complex Receivers¶

For a Complex64 / Complex128 receiver, the real and imaginary parts are drawn independently, each with standard deviation stddev / sqrt(2), so the expected squared distance from the (real) mean is still stddev * stddev. mean shifts the real component; the imaginary component stays centered at zero.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The second parameter is standard deviation, not variance.

  • normal_ fills an existing shape — it does not build one from the parameters. Use randn / normal to create.

  • The receiver dtype must be floating-point or complex; integers are rejected (use random_).

  • Draws are reproducible only if you set pluss::rng_seed(seed) first; each call then advances the stream.

  • Not differentiable — a tracks_slope_ receiver gains nothing from being overwritten with noise.

Summary¶

normal_(mean = 0, stddev = 1) fills the receiver in place with Gaussian samples:

  • receiver supplies shape/dtype/platform/storage; old values are discarded

  • second argument is standard deviation; stddev = 0 gives a constant fill

  • reproducible under pluss::rng_seed(seed); each call advances the stream

  • floating-point or complex dtype only; not differentiable; aliases see the write

See Also¶

  • pluss::series::randn / pluss::series::normal: create a Gaussian tensor instead of filling one.

  • Series::uniform_: bounded continuous fill.

  • Series::log_normal_: fill with exp of normal samples (positive, right-skewed).

  • Series::cauchy_: a heavy-tailed location-scale alternative.

  • Series::random_: integer-valued fill.
